crime_highlights: From early on, Ms. W.'s and J.W.'s hands were tightly tied with zap straps, the latter's by Mr. Lesko.
Both W.s were struck, Ms. W. repeatedly
all three men demanding that they reveal where money was kept, and threatening to kill them if they did not
The W.s repeatedly begged not to be killed
He also fired his gun twice close to Ms. W.'s head.

rationale_highlights: I note, for example, that a family member told the writer of the pre-sentence report that Mr. Lesko was at one stage embarrassed about his Indigenous ancestry.
I note also that from some of the reference letters submitted on Mr. Lesko's behalf, it appears that his upbringing may have been somewhat more difficult for him than he wished the Court to consider
I also take into account Mr. Lesko's Métis heritage and the effects it may have had for him, as well as other challenges he may have faced, as I discussed earlier.
note: Court lists Métis heritage as mitigating but does not say culpability reduced.

crime_highlights: Mr. Thomas's vehicle suddenly crossed the centreline, proceeded diagonally across the northbound lane at a relatively high rate of speed, according to the vehicle's data recorder, and then onto the far shoulder where Kim and Tracy Ward were walking.
Mr. Underwood heard the sound of impact and saw one of the women airborne and eventually coming to rest in the middle of the road.
Ms. Ward had died on impact.
rationale_highlights: both it and the presentence report highlight the damaging and traumatic experience Mr. Thomas's family and community in general have experienced, again because of colonization and the residential school system.

Having considered the circumstances of these offences, Mr. Thomas's personal circumstances, the aggravating and mitigating factors, the Gladue principles, and the fundamental principle of sentencing that any sentence must be proportionate to the gravity of the offence
I am persuaded a term of imprisonment, somewhat less than suggested by the Crown, will properly reflect these factors
note: Court's conclusion is general: sentence somewhat less than Crown sought, reflecting Gladue principles.
